items.title: Meet Diana Zawadzki - Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America
What’s new with Grafana variables: less clutter, easier reuse across dashboards, and more
items.summary: Template variables are one of the most used features in Grafana, providing users with a dropdown to turn one dashboard into hundreds: pick a different cluster , region , or service , and every panel updates. For most of Grafana's history, variables had a single home at the top of the dashboard. Each dashboard had one flat list of variables, and that list was shared by every panel on it. But as dashboards grew in size and number, those controls became harder to organize and maintain. The top of a dashboard could get crowded with dropdowns that only applied to certain panels, while shared controls were copied across dashboards and had to be updated individually. To address these challenges, we’ve rolled out two new features in Grafana: Section-level variables for rows and tabs (generally available): these variables let you place controls near the panels they affect, reducing clutter at the top of the dashboard. items.title: Prometheus v3.16.0
items.summary: - [CHANGE] API: The experimental search endpoints now clamp batch size to 1000. 19731
items.release_notes:
- [CHANGE] API: The experimental search endpoints now clamp `batch_size` to 1000. #19731
- [CHANGE] Configuration: Default --web.external-url to https when --web.config.file enables TLS. #19241
- [CHANGE] PromQL: Subquery samples are now included in the query TotalSamples and TotalSamplesPerStep statistics, and SamplesRead now counts reads from subqueries with an @ modifier in range queries. #19165
- [CHANGE] Remote write: Stop exposing the deprecated `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_total`, `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_failed_total`, `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_retried_total`, and `prometheus_remote_storage_metadata_bytes_total` metrics for Remote Write 2.0 queues. #20080
- [CHANGE] Remote write receiver: Count Remote Write 2.x samples and histograms ingested without metadata in `prometheus_api_remote_write_without_metadata_appended_samples_total` even when `metadata-wal-records` is disabled. #19812
- [CHANGE] TSDB: Reject exemplars whose label names are not unique, instead of storing them and serving a duplicate JSON key from `/api/v1/query_exemplars`. #19896
- [FEATURE] API: Allow overriding PromQL Start Timestamp processing on a per-query basis using the `X-Prometheus-Use-Start-Timestamps` HTTP header. #19066
- [FEATURE] Agent: Support metadata-wal-records in Prometheus Agent mode. #19684
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Add experimental `integral()` function for computing integral-over-time of range vectors behind the `--enable-feature=promql-experimental-functions` flag. #14440
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Add experimental query cost estimation, actual cost reporting, and configurable execution limits, enabled with `--enable-feature=query-cost`. #20028
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Smoothed and Anchored vector selectors are now stable and always-on. #19697
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Use start timestamps to detect counter resets when float timeseries are queried using extended range selector modifiers (`anchored`, `smoothed`). This feature is hidden behind `use-start-timestamps` feature flag. #18966
- [FEATURE] Promtool: print test filename during promtool tests #18271
- [FEATURE] PromQL: Allow unquoted Unicode letters and dots behind a feature flag #20162
- [ENHANCEMENT] Search API: Warn when participating remote-read storage does not support search. #19992
- [ENHANCEMENT] Remote Read: Add native histogram prometheus_remote_read_handler_gate_wait_duration_seconds to measure concurrency-gate wait duration, including requests canceled while waiting. #18355
- [ENHANCEMENT] Remote Write: Add experimental flag `convert_nhcb_to_classic` to convert NHCB to classic histograms for external systems that dont support NHCBs. #17205
- [ENHANCEMENT] promtool: Add `--allow-incompatible-block-duration` so users can specify any max-block-duration instead of being restricted to the default Prometheus block durations. #19363
- [PERF] Remote write: Cache repeated OTLP histogram metric names. #19717
- [PERF] OpenMetrics 2.0 parser: Reuse classic histogram and sum

items.summary: OpenTelemetry JavaScript has released SDK 3.0 ( stable v3.0.0 packages and experimental v0.300.0 packages ) and API 1.10.0 . Migration guide For a detailed description of breaking changes, see the OpenTelemetry JS SDK 3.x migration guide . What is JS SDK 3.x? JS SDK 3.x encompasses new releases of the @opentelemetry/ JavaScript packages published from the opentelemetry-js repository , except the API and semantic-conventions packages. The package versions for this new major will be >=3.0.0 for the stable and >=0.300.0 for the unstable packages. Details on the full list of packages can be found in the migration guide .

items.title: Bridging Alloy and OpenTelemetry: the OTel engine is now in Public Preview
items.summary: Many Grafana Cloud customers love what Alloy offers them, but we're also seeing a growing base of users who feel the same way about the OpenTelemetry Collector. We want to make it easy for customers to make the decision that makes the most sense, regardless of their preference. When we introduced the OpenTelemetry engine for Grafana Alloy , we set out to give teams a way to run native OTLP pipelines without giving up the power and flexibility Alloy is known for. Since then we've kept building: ironing out service installation support, enabling Fleet Management , and folding in feedback from early users. Today, as of Alloy v1.21.0, we're happy to share that the OTel engine has moved into Public Preview , running right alongside the default engine you already know. In this post, we'll dig into when you'd reach for each engine, walk through some of the most interesting use cases we've seen so far, and give a preview of where both engines are headed next. Trace linkage: connect the dots between your app traces and database queries
items.summary: When an application request slows down, a trace can show a database call. Finding the database query behind it can be tedious, requiring you to switch between traces and database telemetry, as well as match timestamps or query text by hand. In Grafana Cloud, the Database Observability app already provides a window into all of your database telemetry, including query samples, performance history, and explain plan. items.title: Only include resource detectors you need by building your own Collector
items.summary: There are many reasons for building your own OpenTelemetry Collector distribution. The existing distributions are designed to be broadly useful, which means they include many more components than what an individual deployment uses. Building your own gives you the ability to select only the components you care about, add your own custom components, and control exactly what ends up in the binary you run in production. One of the reasons I prefer to build my own distribution is to limit the size of the binary I have to ship around and to ensure that the least amount of dependencies are included. Fewer dependencies means a smaller binary, a smaller attack surface, and fewer third-party modules to track when a vulnerability is disclosed. The OpenTelemetry Collector Builder (ocb) makes this possible: you write a manifest file in YAML to select the components you care about, and ocb compiles them into the resulting binary.

items.title: Faster, smaller checkpoints: the File Log receiver now uses protobuf
items.summary: If you run the File Log receiver with a storage extension, the Collector writes a checkpoint every time it polls your log files. That checkpoint is how the receiver remembers where it stopped reading, so a restart does not lose or duplicate logs. For years that checkpoint format was JSON. Starting with OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib v0.164.0, checkpoints are always written as protobuf. On our benchmarks, saving a checkpoint is almost 5 times faster, loading one is more than 5 times faster, and the checkpoint itself is about 35% smaller.

But embracing agents also means embracing the monitoring best practices that have long been part of engineers' workflows: tracking performance, catching errors, and responding to incidents But it doesn't stop there. Agents also introduce new challenges. They can give different answers to the same question, be confidently wrong without throwing an error, and turn one request into a long chain of model and tool calls that’s hard to debug. These components are marked as [Unmaintained](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#unmaintained) and will eventually be removed from our community distributions. If you depend on these components we need your help to support them.

- `connector/service_graph`: Remove stable connector.servicegraph.virtualNode gate (#52239)
- `exporter/prometheus`: Always preserve leading and consecutive underscores in label names. (#50429)
  Remove `-pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization` from `--feature-gates`; disabling this gate now causes a startup error.
  
- `exporter/prometheus_remote_write`: Always preserve leading and consecutive underscores in label names. (#50429)
  Remove `-pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization` from `--feature-gates`; disabling this gate now causes a startup error.
  
- `pkg/azurelogs`: Promote the `pkg.translator.azurelogs.EmitV1LogConventions` and `pkg.translator.azurelogs.DontEmitV0LogConventions` feature gates to beta. (#52096)
  `code.function.name` and `code.file.path` are now emitted instead of `code.function` and `code.filepath` by default.
  The gates no longer control the `event.name` resource attribute, which is always emitted.
  
- `pkg/coreinternal`: Promote internal.coreinternal.goldendataset.DontEmitV0HTTPConventions and internal.coreinternal.goldendataset.EmitV1HTTPConventions feature gates to Beta (#45293, #45089)
  Both feature gates should be promoted together as per RFC.

- `pkg/zipkin`: Promote "pkg.translator.zipkin.EmitV1HttpConventions", "pkg.translator.zipkin.DontEmitV0HttpConventions", "pkg.translator.zipkin.EmitV1ScopeConventions", and "pkg.translator.zipkin.DontEmitV0ScopeConventions" feature gates to Beta. (#50909)

items.title: The case for OpenTelemetry maintainership
items.summary: I believe OpenTelemetry’s primary constraint isn’t ideas, code contributions, or adoption, but maintainers. About me I’ve been working on OpenTelemetry since early 2021. I’m a maintainer of opentelemetry-java, opentelemetry-configuration, and opentelemetry-injector, and a member of the Technical Committee. In that time I’ve worked at two observability companies, New Relic and now Grafana Labs, in roles with a charter to work on OpenTelemetry while also engaging in internal engineering efforts that depend on it. This post is my opinion, informed by involvement in a lot of different OpenTelemetry projects and by watching various contributors come and go.

items.title: VictoriaMetrics v1.155.0
items.release_notes:
## [v1.155.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.155.0)

Released at 2026-10-23

**Update Note 1:** `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): `/admin/tenants` requests without `start` and `end` query args now return tenants for the current day. This is a breaking change because previously it was expected to return all tenants. If you still need to retrieve all tenants, set the `start` and `end` params so that the resulting time range fully includes the `-retentionPeriod`. Also note that [vmctl](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmctl/victoriametrics/) is known to send requests to `/admin/tenants` under the hood when migrating data between VictoriaMetrics deployments. Therefore, make sure that you run `vmctl` with both `*-filter-time-start` and `*-filter-time-end` params. See the updated [URL format](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/#url-format) and [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791) for details.

* SECURITY: upgrade Go builder from Go1.27.2 to Go1.27.3. See [the list of issues addressed in Go1.27.3](https://github.com/golang/go/issues?q=milestone%3AGo1.27.3%20label%3ACherryPickApproved).
* SECURITY: upgrade base docker image (Alpine) from 3.24.2 to 3.24.3. See [Alpine 3.24.4 release notes](https://alpinelinux.org/posts/Alpine-3.21.9-3.22.7-3.23.7-3.24.3-released.html).

* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics components: add `-healthcheck` command-line flag, which checks that the running process accepts connections at `-httpListenAddr` and exits with non-zero code if the check fails. This allows setting up Docker `HEALTHCHECK` in images without `curl` or `wget`. See [these docs](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/url-examples/#health) and [VictoriaLogs#1565](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/issues/1565).
* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics components: expose `process_cpu_cores_host`, `process_cpu_cores_cgroup_quota`, `process_memory_host_bytes` and `process_memory_cgroup_bytes` metrics. Cgroup metrics are `-1` if no cgroup limit is set or the limit cannot be read. See [#11460](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11460).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): deprecate Server URL editing and show a warning when using a saved custom URL. Existing custom URLs continue to work. See [#11735](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11735).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): update the appearance of error, warning, info, and success messages. See [#11736](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11736).

OpenTelemetry Operator v0.162.0
items.release_notes:
## 0.162.0

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `auto-instrumentation`: Block automatic NodeJS instrumentation upgrades across 0.79.0 because of breaking HTTP, network, and database semantic convention changes. (#2542)
  To upgrade, manually set spec.nodejs.image to an image using instrumentation 0.79.0 or higher. See https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-operator/issues/2542 for migration details.

### 🚀 New components 🚀

- `auto-instrumentation`: Add support for auto-instrumentation in PHP applications. (#932)
  Auto-instrumentation in PHP applications is disabled by default in operator. Users can enable it by setting the
  `--enable-php-instrumentation` or `ENABLE_PHP_AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION` environment variable to `true` in operator
  and setting up the annotations `instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/inject-php` and `instrumentation.opentelemetry.io/otel-php-api-version`.
  For more information, please refer to the documentation.
  
- `auto-instrumentation`: Add initial version of autoinstrumentation for ruby (#3762)
  Ruby auto-instrumentation is disabled by default. Enable it with `--enable-ruby-instrumentation=true`.

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `collector`: Inject the cluster TLS profile's supported groups as `curve_preferences` into generated collector configurations. (#6893)
  Receivers and extensions with a `tls` block in `spec.config` now get `curve_preferences` defaulted from the
  cluster's TLS security profile `groups`, following the same defaults-only rule as `min_version` and
  `cipher_suites`: values set by the user are never overridden.
  Groups without a collector `curve_preferences` spelling are logged at operator startup and not injected.
  

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `operator, target allocator, opamp, auto-instrumentation`: Remove the distrusted emSign root CAs from the operator, target allocator, OpAMP bridge, and Python auto-instrumentation images. (#5802)
  The operator, target allocator, and OpAMP bridge images require Alpine `ca-certificates` 20261020-r0 or later.
  The Python auto-instrumentation image requires `certifi` 2026.10.19 or later and is published as `0.66b1-3`.
  The updated CA bundle removes the distrusted eMudhra emSign roots, including `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`.
  Images are built with Go 1.27.3, which includes the `crypto/x509` security fixes released on 2026-10-19.
  
- `collector`: Include the requesting user's UID and extra fields in the SubjectAccessReviews used to check RBAC privilege escalation. (#5659)
  Authorizers that rely on these fields, such as AKS with Azure RBAC for Kubernetes Authorization, denied the check
  for users who held the required permissions.
  
- `collector, target allocator`: Use pointer for TargetAllocator Telemetry field so omitempty works correctly with encoding/json (#5695)
  Go's encoding/json does not omit zero-value structs with omitempty. The non-pointer
  TelemetryConfig field caused targetAllocator.telemetry to always be serialized du

Understanding how people use them will help us focus our efforts within the maintainer time available. Which pages are affected? We have frozen new entries and updates to the following lists while we consider retiring or changing them: Registry : libraries, Collector components, and other tools for using and extending OpenTelemetry. Vendors : organizations offering solutions that consume OpenTelemetry. Distributions : third-party distributions of OpenTelemetry components. Integrations : software with OpenTelemetry support. Adopters : organizations using OpenTelemetry. The issue describes the current direction for each list, including retiring the registry in favor of the OpenTelemetry Ecosystem Explorer . items.summary: Security patch release
items.release_notes:
Security patch release
----------------------

Out-of-band security patch release to fix CVE-2026-111943 ([golang/go#82345](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/82345)): upgrades Go to 1.26.10 so that the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are no longer trusted, and updates all dependencies to their latest patch versions.

Summary of Changes
------------------

**Minor Changes:**
* alibabacloud: support RRSA (RAM Roles for Service Accounts) credentials in the IPAM allocator, alongside static AccessKeys and ECS instance RAM roles (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49093, @4n4nd)

**Bugfixes:**
* Allow wildcard CIDR selectors to match nodes when --policy-cidr-match-mode=nodes is configured (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#47828, @TheBeeZee)
* bpf: nat: fix outer ICMP checksum for ICMP/SCTP NAT error packets (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#48819, @fds7280)
* CiliumEnvoyConfig now only redirects Services in its own namespace, as documented; service references in CiliumClusterwideEnvoyConfig without a namespace default to "default" again. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49076, @maxskokov)
* datapath: Fix NAT46x64 gateway prefix conversion panic (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49177, @HadrienPatte)
* Fix an issue where terminating backends were evicted from BPF maps when trafficDistribution was enabled. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#48349, @taesung320)
* Fix invalid L4 checksum on IPv6 ClusterIP reverse NAT for CHECKSUM_PARTIAL packets on kernels < 6.12, affecting the case when packets are bridged/tunneled from the client pod to a remote host (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49204, @liuyuan10)
* Fix regression in Cilium 1.20.3 where the Gateway API implementation would incorrectly handle BackendTLSPolicy configurations, leading to high Cilium CPU usage and inability to forward traffic. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49568, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49525, @youngnick)
* Fixes an issue in LBIPAM where on service upsert, if IP allocations are not changed the sharing index is not updated. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#48938, @0xch4z)
* nodediscovery: in IPAM ENI and Azure modes the operator now treats nodes as running in multi-pool mode from the very first event. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49390, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49242, @41ks)
* Reduce transient DNS SERVFAIL/REFUSED for pods that query immediately at startup by pushing/applying Standalone DNS Proxy policy snapshots more frequently (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49112, @QxBytes)
* Remove the unused pebble binary from the cilium image to clear its Go standard library vulnerability findings. (Backport PR cilium/cilium#49474, Upstream PR cilium/cilium#49380, @aanm)

**CI Changes:**
* [v1.20] ci: ignore transient xDS mode

- Add `Sampler.Shutdown` operation.

  allowed after `Shutdown`.

- Specify that `Shutdown` of the periodic exporting MetricReader MUST include
  the effects of `ForceFlush`.
  ([#5305](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5305))

  ([#4995](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/4995))

  unless new `OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_ENTITIES_ENABLED != true`.
  ([#5147](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5147))

## Entities

- Add in-development entity-resource startup specification.
  ([#5057](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5057))
- Remove `OTEL_ENTITIES` from general env var configuration spec.
  ([#5147](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5147))

## Common

- Stabilize Attribute and Attribute Collection representation for non-OTLP.
  ([#5149](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5149))

## OpenTelemetry Protocol

- Clarify that the OTLP exporter timeout bounds the entire batch export,
  including all request attempts and waits between retries, and that earlier
  caller deadlines take precedence.
  ([#5347](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5347))

## Compatibility

- Stabilize Prometheus Unknown-typed metric transformation.
  ([#5213](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5213))
- Stabilize Prometheus Info metric transformation.
  ([#5211](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-specification/pull/5211))

items.title: Strengthening OpenTelemetry security while preserving API stability
items.summary: OpenTelemetry has updated its client versioning policy to make room for security fixes that need to change behavior. Stable SDKs and Contrib components, such as instrumentation libraries and exporters, can now make narrowly scoped, necessary security changes in minor or patch releases, even when those changes affect existing users. Public API compatibility remains protected. The intent is to help users receive security improvements within the major version they already use. Some upgrades may require configuration or operational changes. In such cases, release notes must explain the impact and what to do.

Compatible with OpenSearch and OpenSearch Dashboards version 2.19.7

* Add upper bound for the hot_threads `snapshots` parameter with configurable `monitor.jvm.hot_threads.max_snapshots` cluster setting ([#23144](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/23144))
* Add `search.query.max_query_nesting_depth` setting to limit query_string parenthesis nesting depth and prevent StackOverflowError ([#22854](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22854))

* Disable Mustache partial template resolution in search templates ([#22440](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22440))
* Reject out-of-range WLM node threshold updates at validation time ([#22678](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22678))

### Bug Fixes

* Fix unbounded recursion in JSON and binary deserialization that could cause StackOverflowError ([#22427](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22427))
* Strengthen scroll_id validation to prevent OOM from crafted scroll IDs with oversized counts ([#22401](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22401))
* Validate `base_path` in fs repository to prevent path traversal outside configured `path.repo` directories ([#22381](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22381))
* Fix handling of unsupported zstd HTTP content encoding in netty4 and nio transports ([#23324](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/23324))

* Bump Jackson to 2.18.9 and Log4j to 2.25.5 ([#22990](https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/pull/22990))

items.title: From production problem to proposed fix: Implement autonomous operations with Grafana AI
items.summary: You've just finished a deployment, and though your service is up, you start to notice some requests are getting slower. To address the lag, someone—or, more likely, some group of people on your team—needs to watch the dashboards, decide whether the change matters, investigate what happened, and turn the findings into a fix. At each step you're gathering context—and often explaining that context again to the next person or tool. To make matters worse for the team responsible for the service, all this work is getting in the way of everything else they need to build. With Grafana Assistant in Grafana Cloud, you can bring more of those tasks together in one place, helping you resolve incidents faster so you can get back to building. Released at 2026-10-19

Previously, such requests were delayed by 2-3 seconds before being proxied to `unauthorized_user`, though there were no users to brute-force. ## [1.21.0](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/compare/v1.20.0...v1.21.0) (2026-10-16)


### ⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

* **otelcol.receiver.kafka:** `otelcol.receiver.kafka` and `otelcol.exporter.kafka` `metadata > retry > max_retries` now defaults to `20` (was `3`) and is now actually applied. Upstream's Kafka client silently ignored it since the franz-go migration. `otelcol.exporter.kafka` now also applies `backoff`. ([#7366](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7366))
* **otelcol.connector.signaltometrics:** `otelcol.connector.signaltometrics` `error_mode` now defaults to `ignore` (was `propagate`). A failing OTTL expression now skips the record and logs the error instead of dropping the whole payload. Set `error_mode = "propagate"` to restore the previous behavior. ([#7366](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/issues/7366))
* **loki.write:** `loki.write` configurations that set `wal { enabled = true }` now fail to load unless Alloy runs with `--stability.level=experimental`. To keep using the WAL, add `--stability.level=experimental` to the `alloy run` command. To keep the default stability level, remove the `wal` block or set `enabled = false`. items.summary: Security
items.release_notes:
## Security

- `deps`: Update Go to 1.26.9 (CVE-2026-56858, CVE-2026-56862, CVE-2026-56860, CVE-2026-56859, CVE-2026-56853, CVE-2026-33818, CVE-2026-97031, CVE-2026-94440, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659), google.golang.org/grpc to v1.83.2 (CVE-2026-84445, CVE-2026-84304), github.com/apache/thrift to v0.24.0 (CVE-2026-43871), golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 (CVE-2026-39821, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-46600), golang.org/x/text to v0.42.0 (CVE-2026-56851), golang.org/x/crypto to v0.57.0 (CVE-2026-56854), and the OpenTelemetry log modules to v0.21.0 ([#8099](https://github.com/grafana/tempo/issues/8099)) (@mdisibio)

## Bug fixes

- `live-store`: Fix a panic in live-store `FindTraceByID` when more spans for the trace arrive while it is being combined with block data and marshalled. ([#8111](https://github.com/grafana/tempo/issues/8111)) (@KR-Ravindra)
  The live trace's `Batches` slice was handed to the trace combiner with spare capacity, so the
  combiner's append and the push path's append wrote different batches into the same slot of the
  live trace's backing array. `Size()` and `Marshal()` then saw different objects and marshalling
  panicked with `slice bounds out of range`.
  
- `query-frontend`: Fix rare cache collision between instant and range metrics queries. ([#7290](https://github.com/grafana/tempo/issues/7290)) (@ruslan-mikhailov)

The OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib contains everything in the [opentelemetry-collector release](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/releases/tag/v0.163.0), be sure to check the release notes there as well.

## End User Changelog

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `cmd/opampsupervisor`: The supervisor now fails to start when the deprecated `reports_remote_config` capability option is set to `true`. (#49763)
  Remove `reports_remote_config` from the supervisor config; `accepts_remote_config` enables both the AcceptsRemoteConfig and ReportsRemoteConfig OpAMP capabilities. The option will be removed in v0.165.0.
  
- `connector/failover`: Reject empty `condition.error.contains` values and fail over only for matching downstream errors (#44518)
  `condition.error.contains` now requires a list of non-empty strings.
- `exporter/signalfx`: Exclude generated `container_cpu_utilization` metric by default (#51906)
  This metric has been deprecated in favor of `container.cpu.usage`. If `container_cpu_utilization`
  is still required, please add it to the exporter's `include_metrics` configuration option as shown below.
  ```
  signalfx:
    include_metrics:
      - metric_name: container_cpu_utilization
  ```
  
- `extension/google_cloud_logentry_encoding`: Fix Cloud DNS query logs failing to decode when `vmInstanceId` is in exponent notation. `host.id` is now a string taken from `vmInstanceIdString` instead of an int taken from `vmInstanceId`. (#51552)
- `processor/redaction`: Keep every redaction summary attribute intact when data re-enters the processor (#50770)
  Only five of the fourteen summary attributes the processor writes survived a second redaction processor. When data
  passed through one, `redaction.allowed.keys`, `redaction.allowed.count` and the seven `redaction.body.*` attributes
  were treated as unknown keys, deleted, and reported in `redaction.redacted.keys`.
  
  The processor now treats all fourteen as its own bookkeeping rather than as user data, so they are no longer deleted,
  masked, obfuscated or counted as redacted, and the summary accumulates across chained processors as intended.
  Previously a `blocked_key_patterns` or `blocked_values` rule matching one of these attributes replaced the summary
  with a masked value, and with `redact_all_types` enabled it rewrote the `*.count` integers as strings, which made the
  running totals read back as zero at the next hop.
  
  Chaining two processors also reported the same attribute more than once: the allowed and ignored summaries
  describe the record as it currently stands, which every processor re-derives in full, so merging them with an
  upstream value counted one attribute twice. `redaction.allowed.keys` read `email,email` with
  `redaction.allowed.count` of 2 for a single allowed attribute. Those two outcomes now replace the upstream
  value, while the redacted and masked outcomes keep accumulating, because a removed key and an already masked
  value cannot be dete

## End User Changelog

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `cmd/builder`: Add `dist.resource.detection.detectors` to the builder config, letting distributions opt into a smaller set of resourcedetectionprocessor detectors via generated go build tags. (#16075)
- `cmd/mdatagen`: Generate exporter queue/batch sender defaults from an opt-in `sending_queue` field in metadata.yaml. See the [batching migration RFC](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/rfcs/batching-migration.md). (#15963)
  Declaring `sending_queue` is opt-in; an exporter that omits it is unaffected until it explicitly opts in one at a time during Phase 2 of the migration. Set MDATAGEN_SENDING_QUEUE_OPT_OUT=true to generate the standard default for every undeclared exporter while auditing a whole repository.
- `pkg/pprofile`: Implement Profiles development-version metadata in the OTLP receiver and exporters. (#16147, #16009)
  The receiver rejects malformed, repeated, or unsupported versions before decoding.
  OTLP exporters send the version associated with their compiled-in Profiles schema.
  The version is not configurable, and existing clients without metadata identify
  the initial development version.
  

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `cmd/mdatagen`: Replace the O(n) scan in generated `recordDataPoint` with an O(1) hash lookup, fixing an O(n²) cost per scrape when many data points land on one resource. (#15912)
- `cmd/mdatagen`: When both migration gates are enabled, only the latest metric with its v1 attributes is emitted (legacy attributes are no longer included). (#15979)

- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Drop only the oversized profile when splitting a profiles batch, instead of discarding every profile queued behind it (#16087)

- `pkg/pprofile`: Use the profiles dictionary for resource and scope attribute strings sent over OTLP/gRPC. (#15861)
  The OTLP/gRPC profiles client now interns attribute strings before transmission, matching the OTLP/HTTP path. The server resolves the references before exposing pdata to consumers.
  
- `pkg/xpdata`: Fix `xhash` producing the same hash for different maps by length-prefixing keys, strings and bytes. (#16048)
  All hash values produced by `xhash` change.

## 0.161.0

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `opamp`: Use the Kubernetes cluster ID to compute standalone OpAMP Bridge agent instance IDs. (#5689)
  - Existing standalone agents will report new instance IDs after upgrade.
  - The bridge now requires the "get" permission on the "kube-system" namespace to read the cluster ID.
  
- `collector`: Remove the deprecated `--create-rbac-permissions` CLI flag. RBAC permission creation is now exclusively autodetected at startup. (#2588)
  The flag was deprecated in v0.88.0. The operator now always autodetects whether its service account can create ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings.

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `collector`: Add `revisionHistoryLimit` field to OpenTelemetryCommonFields to control the number of old ReplicaSets retained for Deployment and StatefulSet workloads, and for the TargetAllocator Deployment. (#0)
- `collector`: Skip the automatic `GOMEMLIMIT` and `GOMAXPROCS` environment variables when the collector config enables the `cgroup_runtime` extension. (#5651)
  The extension sets both variables from the cgroup limits and does nothing when they are already present.
  The deprecated `cgroupruntime` type name is recognized as well.
  Each variable is skipped only while its `gomemlimit.enabled` or `gomaxprocs.enabled` setting is true.
  
- `collector, target allocator`: Add `imagePullSecrets` to the OpenTelemetryCollector and TargetAllocator CRs, passed through to the pod spec of the generated workloads. A target allocator embedded in an OpenTelemetryCollector uses the collector's `imagePullSecrets`. (#4376)
- `collector`: Register the `webhook_event` receiver (alias `webhookevent`) so the operator derives its Service port from `endpoint`, which the receiver requires, and rejects a configuration that omits it. (#5631)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `collector`: Fix the collector defaulting webhook panicking when `receivers` or `exporters` is missing. (#5735)
  The request is now rejected by CRD validation, as it already was when no component defaults apply.
- `target allocator`: Honor the cumulative temporality preference for counters bridged from the Prometheus registry in OTLP self-telemetry. (#5700)
  Bridged counters, such as the Prometheus service discovery metrics, were converted to delta regardless of

## [v1.154.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.154.0)

Released at 2026-10-12

**Update Note 1:** [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): setups with two chained `vmauth` instances, where the first one authenticates requests via `users` and the second one proxies them via `unauthorized_user` (for example, `VMDistributed` or `VMCluster` managed by [VictoriaMetrics operator](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/operator/)), get an extra 2-3 seconds delay for every request. This is because the second `vmauth` receives the `Authorization` header forwarded by the first one and treats it as an invalid auth token. Upgrade to the [v1.154.1](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/docs/victoriametrics/changelog/CHANGELOG.md#v11541) release, where requests aren't delayed if no `users` are configured, or remove the `Authorization` header at the first `vmauth` with `headers: ["Authorization:"]`. See [#11774](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11774).

**Update Note 2:** `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): `/admin/tenants` requests without `start` and `end` query args (or with zero values) can cause excessive memory usage and OOM crashes of `vmstorage`. Such requests are issued automatically by [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui) when it is opened via `vmselect`. This is because `vmstorage` [no longer switches to the global index](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/commit/742778ebf1) for queries with long time ranges, so it scans per-day indexes for every day in the whole retention concurrently. Upgrade to [v1.155.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.155.0), or roll back to [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0). See [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791).

**Update Note 3:** [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): queries and requests to `/api/v1/series`, `/api/v1/labels` and `/api/v1/label/.../values` with long time ranges can cause excessive memory usage and OOM crashes. This is because VictoriaMetrics [no longer switches to the global index](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/commit/742778ebf1) for searches with long time ranges, so it scans per-day indexes for every day in the requested time range concurrently. items.title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry interoperability in 2026: Survey results
items.summary: We ran a survey asking users of OpenTelemetry and Prometheus how they collect, process, and store metrics. The goal was to understand, with real usage data rather than assumptions, how far the ecosystem has moved and whether the interoperability still causes friction. Key takeaways Interoperability has measurably improved since our 2024 survey : the average ease-of-use rating rose from 3.1 to 3.6, the equivalent of one in two respondents rating a whole category higher, and the share of respondents finding the two hard to use together fell from 29% to 10%. In infrastructure instrumentation, Prometheus exporters remain the most-used method (72%) with OTel receivers close behind (57%), and nearly half of respondents run both at once rather than migrating from one to the other. In application instrumentation, OTel SDKs are the most-used method at 65% with Prometheus SDKs at 52%, and 41% use only the OTel style of application instrumentation. items.title: OTel-Native by Design - Building Products That Export to Any Observability Stack
items.summary: With contributions from Dan Gomez Blanco (New Relic). If you’re building self-hosted software or a SaaS product, your users will eventually ask to send logs, traces, and metrics to their own observability stack, whether to satisfy compliance, manage costs, or centralize all their observability data in one place. Locking them into your built-in dashboards or limiting exports to certain vendors creates unnecessary friction. Instead, supporting export to any OpenTelemetry (OTel)-compatible backend is a vendor-neutral, future-proof practice that gives users the freedom to choose their observability stack.

items.title: Zero-code trace-log correlation with OBI
items.summary: You get paged. A trace shows a request failing in one of your services, and you know the answer is in the logs — but which log lines belong to that request? If the service never adopted structured logging with trace context, the honest answer is: you grep by timestamp and hope. OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI) can now add that missing trace context to the logs your services already write. Your applications don’t change: no SDK, no logging-library configuration, no application rebuild or redeploy.

items.title: Feedback wanted: Slickfast rendering Grafana panels to images without a browser
items.summary: Hey, everyone. I’m Alex and I built SlickFast, an open-source (AGPL) render engine that turns a JSON chart spec into SVG or PNG without needing a browser. It’s deterministic: the same data always produces byte-identical output. I’ve been testing it against Grafana 13 as a way to get panel images without running a headless browser. A small prototype reads a dashboard and its panel data through the HTTP API (read-only Viewer token), maps core panels to SlickFast charts, and renders the whole board. On Node Exporter Full with real Prometheus data: 124 panels, no unsupported core panels, about 15 ms to render the SVG and 175 ms for a high-resolution PNG. (image) Because it’s just an image, it can go anywhere: alert notifications, email, Slack, e-ink displays, AI agents. The deterministic output also means a report can be fingerprinted and verified later. Questions for people who know this space better than I do: Would this be more useful as a backend plugin, an app plugin, or a standalone service next to Grafana? These components are marked as [Unmaintained](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/component-stability.md#unmaintained) and will eventually be removed from our community distributions. If you depend on these components we need your help to support them.

  Migrate `num_workers` to `sending_queue::num_consumers`, `flush::interval` to
  `sending_queue::batch::flush_timeout`, and `flush::bytes` to
  `sending_queue::batch::max_size` with `sending_queue::batch::sizer` set to `bytes`.
  This also removes `Config.NumWorkers`, `Config.Flush`, and `FlushSettings` from
  the exported Go API.
  
- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Ingest OTel profiles as Elasticsearch (9.6.0) datastreams (#50589)
  In `otel` mapping mode, profiling signals are now written to OTel-native datastreams
  (e.g. `profiling-events-all.otel-default`) that require **Elasticsearch 9.6.0 or later**.
  Sending profiles to an older cluster will result in `index_not_found_exception` errors and data loss.
  Users on Elasticsearch < 9.6.0 must restrict the exporter to ECS mode via `mapping.allowed_modes: [ecs]`.
  
- `exporter/elasticsearch`: Move OTel profiling serializer to `ecsserializer` package and wire `ecs` mapping mode to use it for profiles. (#50589)
- `pkg/ottl`: Remove the stable `ottl.PanicDuplicateName` and `ottl.contexts.enableOTelColContext` feature gates. (#44630, #46437)
- `pkg/prometheus`: Promote the pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization feature gate from alpha to beta, enabling it by default. (#50429)
  Labels starting with a single underscore (e.g. `_foo`) will no longer be
  prefixed with `key_` by default. To restore the previous behavior, disable the
  feature gate: `--feature-gates=-pkg.translator.prometheus.PermissiveLabelSanitization`.
  
- `processor/adaptive_tail_sampling`: Add explicit root-scoped fingerprint selectors (`root.resource.`, `root.scope.`, `root.span.`, `root.any.`) and require `root.` to name an origin. (#51304)
  `root.` is now a position prefix that composes with the `resource`, `scope`, `span` and `any` origins, so a
  fingerprint can read the root span's resource-level at

items.release_notes:
## 0.160.0

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `operator, collector, target allocator`: Disable operator, collector, and target allocator network policies by default. (#5551, #5558, #5621, #5624, #5654)
  The `operator.networkpolicy` and `operand.networkpolicy` feature gates are moved back to alpha and are disabled by default.
  The generated network policies can block API server access on some clusters.
  To keep creating network policies, enable them with `--feature-gates=+operator.networkpolicy,+operand.networkpolicy`,
  or set `spec.networkPolicy.enabled: true` on individual collectors and target allocators.
  

### 🚩 Deprecations 🚩

- `auto-instrumentation`: Remove autoinstrumentation-php image definition from the repository (#932)
  The PHP autoinstrumentation image will be hosted by the packaging SIG.
  The one released image (v0.1.0) of the image in the operator registry will
  eventually be deleted. This image was never used for any functionality shipped by the operator.

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `collector`: Add RBAC support for extracting labels and annotations from CronJobs (and Jobs) via the `k8sattributes` processor. (#5527)
  The operator's own ServiceAccount must itself hold `get`/`list`/`watch` on `batch/jobs` and
  `batch/cronjobs` for this to take effect, since Kubernetes RBAC only lets a ServiceAccount
  grant permissions it already has. This PR also extends the operator's own ClusterRole
  accordingly (`config/rbac/role.yaml`).
  
- `collector, target allocator`: Add `enableServiceLinks` to the OpenTelemetryCollector and TargetAllocator CRs, passed through to the pod spec of the generated workloads. It defaults to true, matching the Kubernetes Pod field. (#5569)
- `operator`: Add support for Kubernetes 1.37 (#5650)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `auto-instrumentation`: Honor Instrumentation CRD/API json tags when loading `--config-file` (no-CRD webhook configs). (#5618)
  Operator Config fields still load with gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (yaml tags). The
  `instrumentations` block is re-parsed with sigs.k8s.io/yaml so embedded API
  types keep their json tags (for example `apacheHttpd`, `imagePullPolicy`,
  `resourceAttributes`, `valueFrom`, `volumeLimitSize`, `configPath`).
  
- `collector`: Preserve TCP and UDP protocols when generating NetworkPolicy ports. (#5611)
- `target allocator`: Use the `.svc` FQDN for the TargetAllocator endpoint injected into the collector's Prometheus receiver so it works on clusters behind an HTTP proxy. (#5586)
  The bare service name (http://<name>-targetallocator:80) does not match the standard NO_PROXY
  entries (.svc, .cluster.local), so Go routes the request through the proxy. Using
  <name>-targetallocator.<namespace>.svc matches NO_PROXY=.svc while staying compatible with
  custom cluster domains (unlike the full .svc.cluster.local endpoint reverted in #3248).
  
- `target allocator`: Restore `promhttp_metric_handler_requests_total` and `promhttp_metric_handler_requests_i

items.release_notes:
## [v1.153.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.153.0)

Released at 2026-09-28

**Update Note 1:** [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), `vmstorage`, `vmselect` and `vminsert` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/), and [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): builds without CGO (pure Go) may fail to read valid data blocks with the `window size exceeded` error. This can break queries, background merges and [native import](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#how-to-import-data-in-native-format), and can make `vmsingle` and `vmstorage` crash. Affected official builds: `darwin`, `windows`, `freebsd`, `openbsd`, `linux/arm`, `linux/ppc64le`, `linux/386`, `linux/s390x`, and `-pure` builds. The `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` builds use CGO and are not affected. Users of affected builds should not upgrade to this release, or should roll back to [v1.152.0](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/changelog/#v11520). items.title: Exploring the OpenTelemetry Instrumentation Ecosystem
items.summary: OpenTelemetry has a lot of pieces: APIs, SDKs, a protocol, semantic conventions, instrumentation, and tools like the Collector. The APIs and protocol define how telemetry is created and exchanged, while instrumentation is what actually observes what happens inside an application and turns it into telemetry. Semantic conventions give the people writing that instrumentation a shared way to describe what they’re observing. The beauty of this approach is that completely separate authors can instrument different libraries, in different languages, and still produce telemetry that follows the same contract. An HTTP request looks like an HTTP request, regardless of which library or language produced it. Users can then build queries, dashboards, and other tooling around that shared understanding. Once we’ve agreed on the conventions, everything should line up.

items.title: Prometheus and OpenTelemetry interoperability in 2026 - Survey results
items.summary: We ran a survey asking users of OpenTelemetry and Prometheus how they collect, process, and store metrics. The goal was to understand, with real usage data rather than assumptions, how far the ecosystem has moved and whether the interoperability still causes friction. Key takeaways Interoperability has measurably improved since our 2024 survey : the average ease-of-use rating rose from 3.1 to 3.6, the equivalent of one in two respondents rating a whole category higher, and the share of respondents finding the two hard to use together fell from 29% to 10%. In infrastructure instrumentation, Prometheus exporters remain the most-used method (72%) with OTel receivers close behind (57%), and nearly half of respondents run both at once rather than migrating from one to the other. In application instrumentation, OTel SDKs are the most-used method at 65% with Prometheus SDKs at 52%, and 41% use only the OTel style of application instrumentation. items.title: OpenTelemetry Operator v0.159.0
items.release_notes:
## 0.159.0

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `target allocator`: Add `none` as an explicit filter strategy and preserve explicitly configured empty strategies. (#5444)
  The Go type of `TargetAllocatorSpec.FilterStrategy` changed to a pointer so typed clients can
  distinguish an unset strategy from an explicitly configured value. The legacy empty value remains
  accepted as an alias for disabling filtering, but new configurations should use `none`.
  The Target Allocator now rejects any other value of `filter_strategy` on startup, and normalizes
  the empty value to `none` when loading its configuration.
  

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `collector`: Add `resizePolicy` to the OpenTelemetryCollector CR to control how the primary container responds to in-place resource resizes. (#5501)
- `opampbridge`: Add explicit proxy configuration for OpAMP Bridge server connections. (#5351)
- `target allocator`: Add an `allocation_strategy_config` section to the target allocator configuration, allowing the per-node fallback strategy to be set via `allocation_strategy_config.per_node.fallback_strategy.name`. (#5183)
  The top-level `allocation_fallback_strategy` option is now deprecated in favor of the new
  strategy-specific configuration. When both are set, the strategy-specific option takes precedence.
  
- `target allocator`: Add API fields to configure the TargetAllocator's OTLP self-telemetry export. (#5047)
  Adds `spec.targetAllocator.telemetry.metrics.readers` on the OpenTelemetryCollector CR and
  `spec.telemetry.metrics.readers` on the TargetAllocator CR. The schema mirrors the OTel
  declarative configuration spec. The operator renders these
  fields into the TargetAllocator ConfigMap consumed by the binary-side OTLP self-telemetry
  support.
  When the `operand.networkpolicy` feature gate is enabled, the TargetAllocator's generated
  NetworkPolicy now leaves egress unrestricted if self-telemetry export is configured, since
  its destination can be an arbitrary (often external) endpoint that can't be scoped with a
  NetworkPolicy IPBlock/selector.
  

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `collector`: Report a `Ready=False` status condition and a Warning event on the OpenTelemetryCollector when the referenced TargetAllocator cannot be fetched or the collector manifests cannot be built, instead of only logging the error in the operator. (#4296)

items.release_notes:
## [v1.152.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.152.0)

Released at 2026-09-11

* SECURITY: upgrade Go builder from Go1.26.6 to Go1.27.1. See [Go 1.27 release notes](https://go.dev/doc/go1.27).
* SECURITY: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): fix authorization bypass in JWT-based routing when `match_claims` values are used. See [GHSA-f99m-22fh-qw96](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/security/advisories/GHSA-f99m-22fh-qw96).
* SECURITY: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): properly escape server-side errors returned by `/metric-relabel-debug` since they could contain parts of user input. This prevents XSS attacks on the `/vmui/#/relabeling` page. See [GHSA-vw10j-rqhg-qff9](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/security/advisories/GHSA-vw9j-rqhg-qff9).

* FEATURE: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): add the `deny_paths` option to `url_map` to reject a subset of paths matched by `src_paths` or other `src_*` options with `403 Forbidden` (`401 Unauthorized` for anonymous requests) instead of enumerating every allowed path. See [#11452](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11452). Thanks to @andriibeee for contribution.
* FEATURE: [alerts-health](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules/alerts-health.yml): split `TooManyLogs` alert into `TooManyErrorLogs` and `TooManyLogs`. `TooManyLogs` now covers only `warn`-level logs and aggregates them per job and instance. `TooManyErrorLogs` fires on `error`, `fatal`, and `panic` logs with per-location granularity, making it easier to identify the exact source of critical log messages. See [#11417](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11417).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): show the range between the minimum and maximum values for each graph line in the legend. See [#11425](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11425). Thanks to @umer901 for contribution.

* BUGFIX: all VictoriaMetrics components: hide values passed to `-pushmetrics.header` in startup logs, `/metrics`, and `/flags`, since they can contain sensitive HTTP headers such as `Authorization` and API keys. See [#11545](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11545).
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/) and `vminsert` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): fix insert requests getting stuck after another insert request times out, causing clients to time out while waiting

items.title: Seeking Grafana guidance on whether a Community App Plugin can safely rely on the public EmbeddedDashboard API while it remains marked @alpha.
items.summary: I’m developing a Grafana Community App Plugin intended for eventual submission to the Grafana Plugin Catalog. The app needs to render an existing Grafana dashboard by UID inside the plugin without requiring users to manually reconstruct their dashboards. The public EmbeddedDashboard export from @grafana/runtime provides the capability I need, and I have validated it with Grafana 13.2. However, the TypeScript declaration currently marks EmbeddedDashboard as @alpha . For a Grafana Community App Plugin, is it considered acceptable for the core workflow to depend on the public @grafana/runtime EmbeddedDashboard export while it is marked @alpha , or would Grafana recommend avoiding that dependency for a plugin intended for Catalog publication? I’m primarily trying to understand the expected plugin-development/publication boundary before building more of the product around this API. 2 posts - 2 participants Read full topic

## End User Changelog

### 🚩 Deprecations 🚩

- `pkg/confighttp`: Deprecate flat keepalive fields in client and server config in favor of the new `keepalive` section. (#14020)
  The following client configuration fields are deprecated in favor of the `keepalive` section:
    - `idle_conn_timeout` -> `keepalive::idle_conn_timeout`
    - `max_idle_conns` -> `keepalive::max_idle_conns`
    - `max_idle_conns_per_host` -> `keepalive::max_idle_conns_per_host`
    - `disable_keep_alives: true` -> `keepalive::enabled: false`
  The following server configuration fields are deprecated in favor of the `keepalive` section:
    - `idle_timeout` -> `keepalive::idle_timeout`
    - `keep_alives_enabled: false` -> `keepalive::enabled: false`
  Deprecated fields set in the configuration keep working exactly as before and produce a
  deprecation warning when the client or server is created. Setting deprecated fields together
  with the new `keepalive` section is an error.
  Code migrating off the deprecated fields can use the new `NewDefaultKeepaliveClientConfig`
  and `NewDefaultKeepaliveServerConfig` functions to build a `keepalive` section with the
  default values.
  

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `all`: Bump go version in all go.mod to 1.26.0, drop support on 1.25.0 (#15799)
- `all`: Declare windows/amd64 tier 1 and windows/arm64 tier 2 support (#15786)
- `pkg/confmap`: Remove dead `isStringyStructure` helper (unused since (#12793)
  This is an internal, unexported code path with no user-facing behavior change.
  
- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Cache the request size per sizer type so byte-sized batching no longer recomputes the serialized proto size of the whole accumulated batch on every consumed request. (#12636)
  With `sizer: bytes`, the batcher's MinSize check called `BytesSize()`, which
  ignored the cached size and re-walked the entire batch's protobuf on every
  consumed request, making accumulation O(n^2) in the number of merged requests.
  The size is now cached separately for the bytes and items dimensions and
  maintained incrementally during merge/split, so the check is O(1). A single
  untyped cache could not be reused safely because the batcher and the queue may
  ask for different sizer types on the same request.
  
- `processor/memory_limiter`: Only report memory limiter component health status when the health state changes. (#15751)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `cmd/mdatagen`: Allow underscores in feature gate IDs for compatibility with component names with underscores (#15592)
- `pkg/pprofile`: add bounds checks to FromLocationIndices and switchDictionary (#15697)
  FromLocationIndices now returns an error instead of panicking on an out-of-range or
  negative location index, mirroring FromAttributeIndices.
  The index checks used when merging profiles now also reject negative indices. These
  were previously reachable with a negative index de

items.release_notes:
## 0.158.0

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `operator, collector, target allocator`: Enable operator, collector, target allocator network policies by default. (#5394)
  Feature gate `operator.networkpolicy` and `operand.networkpolicy` are promoted to beta, and enabled by default.
  These feature gates create network policies for the operator and operand components.

- `auto-instrumentation`: Apache and nginx instrumentations forward Spec env vars to attach init containers so kubelet can expand $(VAR) references in exporter endpoints. (#5333)
- `collector`: promote the operator.collector.usedefaulttelemetryshape feature gate to stable, so the operator-injected Prometheus telemetry reader always uses collector defaults for without_type_suffix, without_units, and without_scope_info (#5075)
  The gate is now stable and can no longer be disabled. Users wanting the
  pre-v0.154.0 metric name shape should explicitly set
  `without_type_suffix`, `without_units`, and `without_scope_info` to `false`
  in their collector configuration. The gate will be removed in a future release.
- `collector`: moves operator.golang.flags to stable setting GOMEMLIMIT and GOMAXPROCS automatically (#5455)

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `collector`: Fix the automatic-upgrade routine binding two Prometheus readers to the same port when a collector already uses `service.telemetry.metrics.readers`. (#5416)
  When an OpenTelemetryCollector already configured `service.telemetry.metrics.readers`
  (added by earlier defaulting), the automatic version-upgrade routine still backfilled the
  older, deprecated `address` field for it. The 0.122.0 upgrade step then migrated `address`
  into a new reader, leaving two readers bound to the same host:port. The collector then
  failed to start with "address already in use". The 0.111.0 step now skips backfilling
  `address` when `readers` is already configured, and the 0.122.0 step now skips adding a
  reader for `address` if an equivalent one already exists.
- `collector`: Add PersistentVolume and PersistentVolumeClaim RBAC rules for k8s_cluster receiver automatic RBAC generation. (#5421)
- `auto-instrumentation`: Default `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` to `otlp` for Node.js auto-instrumentation so metrics are exported without extra configuration. (#3768)
  The Node.js SDK only initializes its metrics pipeline when a metric reader is configured, and the
  webhook was not setting one. As a result, metrics silently stopped being exported for anyone relying
  on the previous default behavior. The webhook now sets `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp` by default,
  matching the existing behavior for Python auto-instrumentation, unless the user already set it.

items.title: Uncached I/O in Prometheus
items.summary: Do you find yourself constantly looking up the difference between container memory usage bytes , container memory working set bytes , and container memory rss ? Pick the wrong one and your memory limits lie to you, your benchmarks mislead you, and your container gets OOMKilled. You're not alone. There is even a 9-year-old Kubernetes issue that captures the frustration of users. The explanation is simple: RAM is not used in just one way. One of the easiest things to miss is the page cache semantics. For some containers, memory taken by page caching can make up most of the reported usage, even though that memory is largely reclaimable, creating surprising differences between those metrics. NOTE: The feature discussed here currently only supports Linux. Prometheus writes a lot of data to disk. It is, after all, a database. But not every write benefits from sitting in the page cache. items.title: Introducing the Experimental info() Function
items.summary: Enriching metrics with metadata labels can be surprisingly tricky in Prometheus, even if you're a PromQL wiz! The PromQL join query traditionally used for this is inherently quite complex because it has to specify the labels to join on, the info metric to join with, and the labels to enrich with. The new, still experimental info() function, promises a simpler way, making label enrichment as simple as wrapping your query in a single function call. In Prometheus 3.0, we introduced the info() function, a powerful new way to enrich your time series with labels from info metrics. What's special about info() versus the traditional join query technique is that it relieves you from having to specify identifying labels , which info metric(s) to join with, and the ("data" or "non-identifying") labels to enrich with. Note that "identifying labels" in this particular context refers to the set of labels that identify the info metrics in question, and are shared with associated non-info metrics. items.title: Visualizing Target Relabeling Rules in Prometheus 3.8.0
items.summary: Prometheus' target relabeling feature allows you to adjust the labels of a discovered target or even drop the target entirely. Relabeling rules, while powerful, can be hard to understand and debug. Your rules have to match the expected labels that your service discovery mechanism returns, and getting any step wrong could label your target incorrectly or accidentally drop it. To help you figure out where things go wrong (or right), Prometheus 3.8.0 just added a relabeling visualizer to the Prometheus server's web UI that allows you to inspect how each relabeling rule is applied to a discovered target's labels. Let's take a look at how it works! Using the relabeling visualizer If you head to any Prometheus server's "Service discovery" page (for example: https://demo.promlabs.com/service-discovery ), you will now see a new "show relabeling" button for each discovered target: Clicking this button shows you how each relabeling rule is applied to that particular target in sequence: The visualizer shows you: The initial labels of the target as discovered by the service discovery mechanism.

This blog post will answer some frequently asked questions about the 2.43 release and the stringlabels optimizations. What is the stringlabels release? The stringlabels release is a Prometheus 2.43 version that uses a new data structure for labels. It stores all the label/values in a single string, resulting in a smaller heap size and some speedups in most cases. These optimizations are not shipped in the default binaries and require compiling Prometheus using the Go tag stringlabels . Why didn't you go for a feature flag that we can toggle? We considered using a feature flag but it would have a memory overhead that was not worth it. items.title: Introducing Prometheus Agent Mode, an Efficient and Cloud-Native Way for Metric Forwarding
items.summary: Bartek Płotka has been a Prometheus Maintainer since 2019 and Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat. Co-author of the CNCF Thanos project. CNCF Ambassador and tech lead for the CNCF TAG Observability. In his free time, he writes a book titled "Efficient Go" with O'Reilly. Opinions are my own! What I personally love in the Prometheus project, and one of the many reasons why I joined the team, was the laser focus on the project's goals. Prometheus was always about pushing boundaries when it comes to providing pragmatic, reliable, cheap, yet invaluable metric-based monitoring. Prometheus' ultra-stable and robust APIs, query language, and integration protocols (e.g. Remote Write and OpenMetrics ) allowed the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) metrics ecosystem to grow on those strong foundations. items.title: Introducing the '@' Modifier
items.summary: Have you ever selected the top 10 time series for something, but instead of 10 you got 100? If yes, this one is for you. Let me walk you through what the underlying problem is and how I fixed it. Currently, the topk() query only makes sense as an instant query where you get exactly k results, but when you run it as a range query, you can get much more than k results since every step is evaluated independently. This @ modifier lets you fix the ranking for all the steps in a range query. In Prometheus v2.25.0, we have introduced a new PromQL modifier @ . Similar to how offset modifier lets you offset the evaluation of vector selector, range vector selector, and subqueries by a fixed duration relative to the evaluation time, the @ modifier lets you fix the evaluation for those selectors irrespective of the query evaluation time. The credits for this syntax goes to Björn Rabenstein . @ @ @ The is a unix timestamp and described with a float literal. As we want to be bolder in experimentation, we are planning to use feature flags more. Starting with v2.25.0, we have introduced a new section called disabled features which have the features hidden behind the --enable-feature flag. You can expect more and more features getting added to this section in the future releases. items.title: Remote Read Meets Streaming
items.summary: The new Prometheus version 2.13.0 is available and as always, it includes many fixes and improvements. You can read what's changed here . However, there is one feature that some projects and users were waiting for: chunked, streamed version of remote read API . In this article I would like to present a deep dive of what we changed in the remote protocol, why it was changed and how to use it effectively. Remote APIs Since version 1.x, Prometheus has the ability to interact directly with its storage using the remote API . This API allows 3rd party systems to interact with metrics data through two methods: Write - receive samples pushed by Prometheus Read - pull samples from Prometheus Both methods are using HTTP with messages encoded with protobufs . The request and response for both methods are compressed using snappy . Remote Write This is the most popular way to replicate Prometheus data into 3rd party system. items.title: Subquery Support
items.summary: Introduction As the title suggests, a subquery is a part of a query, and allows you to do a range query within a query, which was not possible before. It has been a long-standing feature request: prometheus/prometheus/1227 . The pull request for subquery support was recently merged into Prometheus and will be available in Prometheus 2.7. Let’s learn more about it below. Motivation Sometimes, there are cases when you want to spot a problem using rate with lower resolution/range (e.g. 5m ) while aggregating this data for higher range (e.g. max over time for 1h ). Previously, the above was not possible for a single PromQL query. If you wanted to have a range selection on a query for your alerting rules or graphing, it would require you to have a recording rule based on that query, and perform range selection on the metrics created by the recording rules. Example: max over time(rate(my counter total[5m])[1h]) . items.title: Implementing Custom Service Discovery
items.summary: Prometheus contains built in integrations for many service discovery (SD) systems such as Consul, Kubernetes, and public cloud providers such as Azure. However, we can’t provide integration implementations for every service discovery option out there. The Prometheus team is already stretched thin supporting the current set of SD integrations, so maintaining an integration for every possible SD option isn’t feasible. In many cases the current SD implementations have been contributed by people outside the team and then not maintained or tested well. We want to commit to only providing direct integration with service discovery mechanisms that we know we can maintain, and that work as intended. For this reason, there is currently a moratorium on new SD integrations. However, we know there is still a desire to be able to integrate with other SD mechanisms, such as Docker Swarm. items.summary: Nearly one and a half years ago, we released Prometheus 1.0 into the wild. The release marked a significant milestone for the project. We had reached a broad set of features that make up Prometheus' simple yet extremely powerful monitoring philosophy. Since then we added and improved on various service discovery integrations, extended PromQL, and experimented with a first iteration on remote APIs to enable pluggable long-term storage solutions. But what else has changed to merit a new major release? Prometheus 2.0 Prometheus has a simple and robust operational model that our users quickly learn to love. Monitored environments have become increasingly more dynamic. More and more we felt the strain this put on Prometheus' performance. items.title: Prometheus 2.0 Alpha.3 with New Rule Format
items.summary: Today we release the third alpha version of Prometheus 2.0. Aside from a variety of bug fixes in the new storage layer, it contains a few planned breaking changes. Flag Changes First, we moved to a new flag library, which uses the more common double-dash -- prefix for flags instead of the single dash Prometheus used so far. Deployments have to be adapted accordingly. Additionally, some flags were removed with this alpha. The full list since Prometheus 1.0.0 is: web.telemetry-path All storage.remote. flags All storage.local. flags query.staleness-delta alertmanager.url Recording Rules changes Alerting and recording rules are one of the critical features of Prometheus. But they also come with a few design issues and missing features, namely: All rules ran with the same interval. We could have some heavy rules that are better off being run at a 10-minute interval and some rules that could be run at 15-second intervals.
